rationale: Ground truth centers on two threads: incomplete/inconsistent validation data (host topology, driver/CUDA/PyTorch versions, warmup method) and unresolved Ref2VA testing status. Y directly hits both — it explicitly demands the missing vLLM-Omni/PyTorch version pin (near-exact match to the ground-truth ask), scrutinizes the validation methodology (1Hz sampling undersampling, unidentifiable memory-model fit), and raises multiple concrete Ref2VA reliability gaps (broken restart command, OOM risk, missing warnings) — while X only tangentially touches these via the Ref2VA curl and peak-memory findings. Both candidates independently converge on the same Ref2VA curl-format bug and the dangling 'RTX PRO 5000' reference, which cross-validates precision for both, but Y's much larger finding set is still well-grounded and more actionable (specific line numbers, code citations, ready-to-use fixes), giving it a clear edge in recall and actionability with only a marginal precision cost from its greater volume.
